transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um, well... what really made me actually come in and make this appointment, like the main thing, is just this whole situation at my job. I work as a wholesale buyer, right? So I deal with a lot of different vendors, a lot of inventory, coordinating product launches, stuff like that. It's a lot of moving parts and a lot of pressure. But lately... well, I just can't shake this feeling. And it's a really intense, constant feeling that the people at work, and honestly even some of the external vendors we contract with, are tracking my specific buys. 

Like, they are watching every single purchase order I put through and coordinating with each other. And they are actively messing with the launch numbers. The data that comes back after a product drops, they are altering it just to make me look completely stupid in front of the whole department. I've tried to explain this to my supervisor, I really have. I sat down with him and laid it all out, and he pulled up the backend reports and the spreadsheets and went through them line by line to try and show me that the numbers don't prove anything fishy is going on. He told me the data is perfectly normal and that I'm doing fine, but I just... I know what I'm seeing, you know? It's just this constant feeling that they're plotting against me, and even if the reports look fine on his screen, I know they're manipulating things behind my back, and it's just making it impossible to do my job right now.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual lately and still feeling full of energy?

Yeah, actually, that's... that's a whole other thing. Sleep has been really weird lately. Or maybe not weird, just... different? Like, there have been plenty of weeks, especially recently with all this work stuff going on, where I sleep maybe three, sometimes four hours a night if I'm lucky. And the crazy thing is, I don't even feel tired! I wake up and I'm just completely wired, like my brain is already running at a hundred miles an hour before my feet even hit the floor. 

I'll just be lying there in the dark, and I'll start thinking about all the purchase orders, the vendors, the inventory tracking, and I'll just realize that lying in bed is honestly just wasting time. It's wasting time I could use to make moves, you know? Like, I could be getting ahead of whatever they're planning, checking the backend systems myself before they have a chance to alter the morning reports. So I just get up. I'll be up at 3:00 AM, pacing around my apartment, making coffee, going through spreadsheets on my laptop, cross-referencing vendor emails from three months ago to see if I can find the discrepancies. I mean, why sleep when I have all this energy and there's so much I need to figure out? My roommate thinks I'm crazy for being up that early, vacuuming or reorganizing the kitchen cabinets while I'm on hold with an overseas supplier, but I just don't need the rest. I feel completely charged up, like I've had a full eight hours, even though the clock says otherwise. It's just... I have too much to do to be sleeping.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually high or euphoric?

Well, yeah, actually. It's like... it's like this massive wave, you know? I get these stretches, these periods where I just feel... incredible. Like I'm on top of the world. It’s this intense rush, like the whole city is just opening up for me, like every traffic light is green and every idea I have is pure gold. I’ll be walking down the street and I just feel this buzz, this absolute certainty that I am exactly where I need to be and everything is just clicking into place perfectly. It's better than a good mood, it's like I'm vibrating with it. 

But the thing is, it doesn't always stay like that, or maybe it does but it just shifts? Because when I'm feeling that good, that dialed in, and then someone at work—like my supervisor, or one of the junior buyers—if they question a purchase order I just put through, or if they tell me I need to slow down or double-check my numbers... man, it just flips. I go from feeling like a king to just being instantly furious. I mean, I snap way harder than I mean to. I’ll yell, or I’ll just completely dress them down right there in the middle of the office, because how dare they, right? When I'm operating on that high of a level, seeing things so clearly, and they want to drag me down with their petty questions about a spreadsheet? It's just so frustrating. So yeah, I feel amazing, really high up there, but it comes with this edge where if anyone gets in my way or doubts me, I just explode on them before I can even stop myself. It's like the energy has to go somewhere, you know?
Have you been feeling that you have special powers, exceptional abilities, or a unique importance that other people don’t recognize?

Well, yeah, actually. I mean, it’s funny you phrase it like that, "special powers," because I wouldn't call it magic or anything, but... I do get this absolute, crystal-clear conviction about things. Especially with my job. Like, I’ll be sitting there, maybe it's 4:00 AM and I'm looking at the overseas manufacturing data, and suddenly it all just connects. I start believing—no, I *know*—that I can spot the next huge trend before anyone else in L.A. even has a clue. 

And I'm not just talking about, you know, guessing what color is going to be popular next spring. I'm talking about this deep, undeniable certainty that the whole sneaker market, the entire industry ecosystem, is basically just waiting on my decisions. It’s like I hold the keys to the kingdom. I’ll look at a prototype for a new drop and I just know, instantly, that if I put the order through, it’s going to shift the entire cultural landscape. And the crazy part is, on paper, I'm still one of the junior buyers. I don't have the title yet, I don't have the corner office, but in my head, during those moments, I am the absolute center of the universe for wholesale retail. 

I try to explain this to the senior guys, you know? I’ll burst into a meeting and tell them, "Look, if we don't corner the market on this specific silhouette right now, we're going to miss the wave that I am personally orchestrating." And they just look at me like I'm out of my mind. They tell me to stay in my lane, stick to the spreadsheets, but they just don't get it. They don't have the vision. They don't see how every single thread connects back to me and the choices I'm making. It’s frustrating because I have this... this gift, this exceptional ability to read the market matrix, and they just treat me like I'm some kid fresh out of high school who doesn't know how the real world works. But I do know. I see it all.
Have there been times when you still believed people at work were plotting against you even when you were not feeling especially high or energized?

Yeah, definitely. It's not just when I'm, you know, totally wired and pacing around the apartment at 3:00 AM. There was actually this period—I think it was maybe a month or two ago?—where I was actually sleeping pretty okay. Like, I was getting a solid six or seven hours, not feeling that massive rush, not feeling like I was the undisputed king of the sneaker market. I was just... going to work, doing my job, feeling pretty level. But even then, even during that calmer stretch, I couldn't shake this feeling. 

For a good few weeks, I was absolutely convinced that the senior guys were still tracking my buys. I'd sit at my desk, feeling totally normal energy-wise, but I'd be looking at the network logs on my computer, just knowing they were monitoring my keystrokes, trying to figure out my strategy so they could steal my vendor contacts and push me out. And the voice, too. Even when I was sleeping fine and not feeling high at all, I'd still be back in the stockroom doing inventory, just trying to count boxes, and I'd hear that voice. Clear as day, just whispering about how they were adjusting the numbers behind my back, how they were setting me up to take the fall for the Q3 deficit. It's so weird because I wasn't amped up, I wasn't angry or euphoric, I was just... there. But the paranoia, or whatever you want to call it, and that voice in the stockroom, they didn't go away just because I finally got some sleep. They just kind of hung around, like a shadow, you know? Like they were just waiting for me to slip up, regardless of how much energy I had. It's exhausting, honestly, always having to look over your shoulder, even on a regular Tuesday when you're just trying to drink your coffee and match up purchase orders.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or felt people were plotting against you, while not feeling especially high, irritable, or depressed?

Yeah, exactly, like I was just saying a minute ago, it was definitely like that. It was for sure longer than two weeks—probably a good three or four weeks, actually. And just to be clear, because I know you're asking about the whole mood thing, I wasn't down in the dumps either. Like, I wasn't depressed at all. I wasn't dragging myself out of bed or feeling hopeless or anything like that. 

I was just... completely baseline. Like a totally average guy doing his routine. I was getting my regular sleep, making my coffee, taking the bus, doing my job... just normal. I wasn't irritable, and I definitely wasn't on that massive high where I feel like I'm running the entire wholesale market and predicting the future of retail. But even during that calmer stretch, with my mood being completely level, I still spent those few weeks absolutely convinced they were tracking my buys. 

It was the weirdest thing because I'd sit at my desk feeling perfectly fine, not agitated, not sad, not buzzing with energy, but I'd be staring at the monitor thinking, "They're logging this. They're watching every single keystroke so they can steal my strategy." And the voice in the stockroom, like I mentioned, it didn't take a break just because I was finally sleeping normally. I’d be back there organizing the size runs, feeling completely calm, and there it was, just whispering about how I was being set up by the senior guys. So, yeah, for a solid few weeks, I had the voice and the whole tracking thing going on, even though the rest of my brain felt completely, 100 percent normal. It’s honestly so exhausting trying to reconcile feeling totally okay with hearing someone whispering behind a stack of shoeboxes.
For most of the time since these experiences began, have your hearing the voice and feeling watched been present even when your mood felt normal?

Well, if I really look back at the whole timeline, like, since this all really kicked off... it’s actually the opposite, I think. I mean, I know I just spent all that time telling you about that one calm stretch, and it was a real thing, but if we're talking about the *majority* of the time? No. Most of the time since this all started has definitely been taken up by those massive, wired stretches. 

Like, I’m talking about those weeks and months where I’m just completely buzzing, or really irritable, overworking myself into the ground. I'll be pulling all-nighters looking at overseas shipping logs, trying to forecast the sneaker drops, and just feeling so... overconfident, you know? Like my brain is going a million miles an hour and it is just physically hard to slow down. I'll be snapping at the senior guys because they can't keep up with my pace, and I'm just pushing, pushing, pushing. 

So, yeah, those calmer periods—like that normal stretch I was just describing where I was just doing the size runs and actually getting some sleep—those are actually a lot shorter. They're really just these little windows, you know? Like brief little breaks in between all the chaos. But if you look at the whole calendar since all this began, the vast majority of it has been me in that completely elevated, can't-stop-won't-stop, hyper-focused zone. The days where my mood is actually normal and level are definitely just a small fraction of the whole picture. Most of my life lately has just been that high-speed grind.
Have you had a stretch where that unusually high or irritable mood lasted at least one full week?

Yeah, oh man, definitely. A week is nothing, honestly. I get these stretches that go on for way longer than a week where I just... I don't even know how to explain the feeling, but it's like the whole city is just opening up for me, you know? Like I can see all the angles, all the supply chains, all the deals before they even happen. I'll be walking down the street and I just feel this electric hum, like I'm plugged straight into the grid and I'm the only one who really gets how the wholesale market is supposed to operate. I get so keyed up, just overflowing with this intense, raw energy. 

And it's great, right? Until it isn't. Because I'll be in that zone, feeling completely unstoppable for days on end, sleeping maybe two hours a night, and then I'll be at work and one of the senior guys will question a purchase order I put in. Or, worse, someone will tell me I need to slow down or take a breath. And man, I just... I snap. I snap way, way harder than I mean to. I'll just go off on them, completely lose my temper, because how can they not see what I'm seeing? How can they be moving so slow when I'm out here practically predicting the future of retail? So yeah, I definitely get those stretches, and they last well over a week where I'm just riding that massive high and then instantly snapping into this intense irritability if anyone gets in my way or tries to pump the brakes on me. It's like my brain is just redlining the entire time, day after day.
Since these problems first began, has it been at least six months?

Oh, six months? Yeah, definitely. It's been way longer than six months. If I really sit down and map it out—which, you know, I do sometimes when I'm up at 3 AM looking at the purchase logs—it's been going on for about a year and three months now. 

I remember the exact timing because it all started right after the company did this massive reorganization. We had this exclusive sneaker launch coming up, this huge drop that everyone in the market was sweating over. Management completely restructured our department to handle it, moving people around, changing the reporting lines, and suddenly I had all this new responsibility. I was trying to track the incoming shipments, dealing with the vendors, and that’s right around when the whole thing kicked off—the buzzing energy, the voice in the stockroom, the feeling that they were logging my keystrokes to steal my buying strategies. 

It was like, before that reorg, I was just a regular guy doing my job, but once that sneaker launch hit the calendar and they shuffled us all around... man, that was the catalyst. That was about 15 months ago, roughly. So yeah, we are well past the six-month mark. It’s just been this crazy rollercoaster ever since that specific launch. I can still picture the exact email they sent out about the restructuring, and it’s like my brain just shifted gears that exact week and hasn't really stopped since.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed? Like, really down and out for two whole weeks? Honestly, I don't think so. I mean, I know guys in the industry who get like that, especially after a bad quarter or when a huge deal falls through. They just kind of check out, you know? They stop answering emails, they look like they haven't showered, they just drag themselves through the day. But me? No, I don't really get like that. 

Sure, I have days where I'm exhausted, like when I've been running on those two hours of sleep for a week straight and my body just finally forces me to crash. I'll sleep for, like, fourteen hours, and wake up feeling kind of groggy and maybe a little drained, but it's not like a deep, dark depression. It's just physical exhaustion from moving at warp speed for so long. And even then, it doesn't last. Give me a day or two to catch my breath, maybe drink an ungodly amount of espresso, and I'm right back in it, looking at the shipping manifests and trying to figure out the next move. 

I don't get that heavy, sad feeling where you just can't get out of bed because what's the point. For me, there's always a point. There's always a new drop, a new angle, a new way to optimize the supply chain. Even when I'm irritable and snapping at the senior guys, it's not because I'm sad, it's because I'm frustrated that they aren't moving fast enough. I'm too keyed up, too focused on the logistics and the numbers to just sit around feeling depressed. So, no, I haven't really had a stretch like that, not for two weeks, not even for a few days really. My brain just doesn't really go in that direction, it's always pushing forward, always looking for the next thing.
During that three- to four-week calmer period, were you still hearing the voice?

Yeah, actually... that’s the weirdest part about all this, to be honest with you. Because you'd think, right? You'd think that once I finally started sleeping normally again—like actually getting a solid seven or eight hours a night instead of just running on fumes, and I stopped feeling like I was single-handedly running the entire wholesale market... you'd think all the other stuff would just switch off, too. 

But it didn't. Not at all. During that whole stretch, which was maybe three or four weeks where my energy was totally level and I was just feeling like a regular guy doing his job, I was still dealing with it. I'd go back into the stockroom to check inventory on the incoming shipments, just doing my normal routine, and I would still hear that voice. Clear as day, just talking away while I'm trying to count shoe boxes. 

And it wasn't just the voice, either. For those few weeks, even though I was completely calm and not keyed up at all, I still spent the whole time believing people were tracking my buys. I'd be looking at my purchase orders on the monitor, and I just knew someone had a keylogger or some kind of backdoor access to my terminal. I kept checking the network logs, looking over my shoulder... because even without that massive high, I still had this absolute certainty that they were monitoring my buying strategies to steal my angles. It's wild because my body felt rested, I wasn't snapping at the senior guys anymore, my brain wasn't redlining... but I'd still be standing there in the back room hearing someone talking to me when nobody was there, and then rushing back to my desk to see if my keystrokes were being recorded. It just wouldn't stop, even when everything else finally slowed down.
About how long was the longest stretch when you were hearing the voice while your mood felt completely normal?

Well, like I was just saying, that whole calmer stretch where I wasn't, you know, totally wired and feeling like I was running the entire wholesale market single-handedly... that lasted for about three or four weeks. And during that entire time, the whole three to four weeks, I was still hearing it. 

It’s really the craziest thing when you stop and think about it, because my mood was totally normal, right? I was sleeping my regular seven or eight hours, I wasn't drinking endless espresso, I wasn't snapping at the senior guys on the floor. I was just coming in, doing my job, feeling completely level-headed. But every single time I went into that stockroom to check the inventory, there it was. The voice. Just talking away. 

And it wasn't just a day or two of it lingering, either. It was that whole three or four-week period. I’d be standing there, completely calm, heart rate normal, just counting boxes of the new drops, and I'd hear it. And then I'd go back to my desk, still feeling totally fine energy-wise, but I'd spend hours checking my terminal because I was absolutely convinced people were tracking my buys. I just knew they were logging my keystrokes. So yeah, the longest stretch where my mood was completely normal but I was still dealing with the voice and the tracking stuff... that was right around three to four weeks. It just didn't let up at all during that time, even though the rest of me felt fine.
At any time, did the voice continue for at least two weeks while your mood felt completely normal?

Yeah, yeah, definitely. Like I said, it was that whole three or four-week stretch. That's definitely more than two weeks, right? So, yes. For that entire time, my mood was, you know, completely normal. I wasn't doing the two-hours-of-sleep thing, I wasn't running around the floor feeling like the king of the wholesale market, I wasn't snapping at the senior guys because they couldn't keep up with my brain. I was just... normal. Calm. Sleeping a solid seven or eight hours, coming in, drinking a normal amount of coffee, just doing my job. 

But even with all that calmness, even with my energy totally leveled out, I still spent that whole few weeks hearing the voice every time I went back into the stockroom. And it's not just the voice, either, it's the whole tracking thing. I spent that whole time, those few weeks, absolutely believing that people were tracking my buys on the terminal. I'd be sitting there, completely calm, heart rate totally fine, but I'd be digging through the network logs because I just knew someone had a keylogger on my system. I was so sure they were trying to steal my angles on the new drops. 

So, yeah, to answer your question, it definitely continued for at least two weeks. It was that whole three to four-week block where I felt totally fine, totally normal, but the voice and the paranoia about the tracking just... they just kept going. It's like my mood hit the brakes, but that other stuff just kept cruising right along at highway speeds. It's really hard to explain to someone who hasn't been there, you know? You're sitting there, feeling fine, but your brain is still telling you someone's talking to you in an empty room and someone's watching your every keystroke. It's wild. But yes, definitely for at least two weeks.
Before these problems started, had you ever heard voices or felt people were plotting against you when your mood was completely normal?

No, no, never. Honestly, before all this started happening recently, I never dealt with anything like that. I mean, I've always been a pretty regular guy, you know? Just went to high school, got my diploma, started working my way up in the wholesale business. I never had any weird stuff going on in my head. 

I remember back when I first started as a junior buyer—this was a couple years ago, way before any of this current mess—I was just focused on learning the ropes, figuring out how the purchase orders worked, getting to know the vendors. My mood was always just... normal. I'd go to work, do my hours, go home, watch some TV, hang out. I never heard anyone talking to me when I was alone in the stockroom back then. The stockroom was just quiet, you know? Just me and the boxes. 

And the whole tracking thing? Not even a blip on my radar back then. I used to just punch in my buys on the terminal, log off, and not give it a second thought. I never once worried that the senior guys or anyone else was trying to steal my angles or put keyloggers on my system. I just trusted the process. It's so crazy to think about how different it was. I was just a regular 22-year-old trying to make a living. So, yeah, before this whole recent situation with the wild energy and then the voices and the tracking... no, I never experienced anything like that when I was just feeling normal. It's all completely new, and honestly, it's pretty terrifying when you compare it to how quiet my life used to be.
At any point, did the voice start when your mood was completely normal, before any high or irritable period began?

Well, let me think back... it's a little hard to untangle it all sometimes, you know? Because everything just kind of bleeds together when you're in the middle of it. But if I really sit down and trace it back... no, I don't think the voice or the tracking stuff started before the high energy kicked in. 

But, I mean, the whole thing—the voice in the stockroom, the absolute certainty that people are logging my keystrokes on the terminal, all of those suspicious beliefs—they've been going on for roughly ten months now. Ten whole months of this. It started around the end of last year, maybe? Yeah, about ten months. And it's just been this constant thing ever since, whether I'm bouncing off the walls and feeling like I own the wholesale market, or whether I'm in that calm, normal stretch like we were just talking about. 

It's just wild to think it's been almost a year of dealing with this. Ten months of looking over my shoulder at the terminal, ten months of dreading going into the stockroom because I know I'm going to hear it. It feels like a lifetime, honestly, but yeah, the timeline is right around ten months for all the suspicious stuff and the voice. But as for it starting *before* I ever got that initial crazy rush of energy and irritability? No, I'm pretty sure the super high energy kind of kicked the door open for everything else, and then the voice and the tracking fears just moved in and stayed for the last ten months.
Altogether, have the voice and the feeling that people were plotting against you lasted for at least one full month?

Oh, definitely. Like I was just saying a minute ago, it's been way, way longer than a month. I mean, honestly, I wish it had only been a month! A month I could probably handle, you know? Like, you can grit your teeth and get through a bad four weeks at the wholesale market. Like when the holiday shipments get backed up or a major vendor screws up a purchase order, you just put your head down and push through it for a month. 

But this isn't just a bad month. Like I mentioned, the suspicious beliefs and the voice have been happening for roughly ten months now. Ten whole months. When you really sit down and think about how many days that actually is... how many times I've had to walk into that stockroom to check inventory and just brace myself, waiting to hear it. Or how many times I've sat at my terminal, totally convinced someone is logging my keystrokes to steal my purchase angles and sabotage my numbers. It's exhausting just talking about it. Ten months of looking over my shoulder every single shift, trying to figure out who's plotting against me while I'm just trying to do my job. 

So, yeah, if you're asking if it's been at least one full month, the answer is a massive yes. It's basically been almost a year of my life just swallowed up by this stuff, day in and day out, whether my mood is totally fine or I'm bouncing off the walls. Ten months of it.
Have you had at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice while your mood felt completely normal?

Yeah, yeah I have. Actually, it's funny you ask about that specific timeframe, because I was just thinking about this stretch... I guess it was a little while back, maybe a couple months ago? I remember it really clearly because, for a second there, I thought maybe I was getting better, or at least getting back to my old self. My energy had finally leveled out. I wasn't waking up at 3 AM with a million ideas for new vendor contracts, and I wasn't talking a mile a minute to the senior buyers. I was actually sleeping through the night, getting a solid seven or eight hours, which was huge for me. I felt... calm. Just normal, regular calm. Not like I was running the whole wholesale market single-handedly, just going in, doing my job, grabbing lunch at the deli across the street, coming back. 

But the thing is, even though my mood was totally fine, completely baseline, the other stuff didn't stop. Not at all. For that whole stretch—it was definitely a few weeks, maybe three or four weeks of just feeling totally regular mood-wise—I was still absolutely convinced that they were tracking my buys on the terminal. I'd sit there, feeling totally calm, but still knowing, just knowing, that someone had a keylogger on my system, watching every purchase order I punched in. And the voice in the stockroom? Still there. I'd go back there to check on a shipment of overstock, feeling completely rested and normal, and I'd still hear it. Just as clear as day. 

It was almost more disturbing that way, honestly. When you're all keyed up and your thoughts are racing, the weird stuff almost fits the vibe, you know? But when you're just sitting there, sipping a coffee, feeling totally fine, and you still hear someone talking to you in an empty room, or you're still terrified to type on your own keyboard... it really messes with your head. So, yeah, there was definitely a period of a few weeks where my mood was totally normal, but the tracking fears and the voice just kept right on going. It didn't take a break just because my energy did.
During that three- to four-week period when your mood felt completely normal, did the voice continue the whole time?

Yeah, yeah, it did. The whole time. Like, every single day of that three or four-week stretch. It’s so strange to think about, really, because you’d assume—or at least I assumed—that if my mood leveled out, if I was finally getting a decent night’s sleep and not waking up at all hours feeling like I had to single-handedly restructure the entire wholesale market... you’d think the other stuff would just fade away, right? Like it was all tied together. 

But it wasn't. Even during that calmer stretch, when I was actually sleeping normally and going into work without that frantic, electric energy... I was still spending all my time believing people were tracking my buys. I’d sit down at my desk with my morning coffee, feeling totally rested, totally fine, and I’d still be staring at the keyboard, absolutely certain someone had rigged it. And the stockroom... man, the stockroom didn't change at all. I’d walk back there to do a routine inventory check, completely calm, not agitated in the slightest, and there it was. The voice. Just as clear as if someone was standing right behind me. 

It didn’t take a day off. Not once during those weeks. It’s almost like... like the voice and the tracking stuff have a mind of their own, completely separate from how I’m actually feeling in my own head. It’s exhausting, honestly, because it makes you realize that even when you feel like you’re doing better, you’re not really free of it. You’re just dealing with it while being less energetic. So, yes, to answer your question, it continued the entire time. Every day of those few weeks, without fail.
At any point, did you hear the voice for a full month while your mood felt completely normal?

Well, a full month? No, I wouldn't say it was a full month. Like I was just saying, it was more like a few weeks. Maybe three or four weeks at the most where my mood was just... regular. Baseline. You know, that stretch where I was finally getting some decent sleep and not waking up feeling like I had to conquer the entire wholesale market before sunrise. 

But even during that calmer stretch, even when I wasn't running on that crazy, electric energy, I still spent those few weeks absolutely convinced that people were tracking my buys on the terminal. And the voice in the stockroom was still there, too. But it wasn't a whole month of feeling normal while that stuff was happening. It was just those few weeks. Because eventually, my mood shifted again. It always does, right? You get this little window where you think, "Okay, I'm just a regular guy going to work, grabbing a sandwich, coming home," but then the energy starts creeping back up, or I get completely dragged down. 

So, no, not a full month of normal mood. Just that three- or four-week window where my energy was fine, but I was still dealing with the tracking and the voice every single day. It's like they're on their own schedule, completely ignoring whether I'm feeling balanced or not. But yeah, the normal mood part? That didn't last a whole month. Just a few weeks.
During the past year, have you ever had two weeks in a row when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed? Like, really down for two weeks straight? No, I don't think so. Not for two weeks in a row, anyway. I mean, sure, I get bummed out sometimes, who doesn't? Especially in wholesale, it can be a real grind, you know? You're constantly dealing with vendors who promise one thing and deliver another, or the logistics get messed up, and you're just sitting there at your desk feeling like you're banging your head against a brick wall. And honestly, dealing with all the tracking stuff... the keylogger on my terminal, the feeling that someone is always watching my purchase orders... that can really drag a guy down. It gets exhausting, it really does. 

There are definitely days where I just feel totally wiped out by it all, where I just want to put my head down on the desk and not talk to anyone. But it's never been like, two solid weeks of just feeling depressed all day, every day. It's more like I'll have a bad day or two where I'm just fed up and tired, but then the energy comes back. Usually, the energy comes back pretty strong, actually. I'll go from feeling totally drained to suddenly realizing I need to overhaul the entire inventory system right this second, and I'll be up for three days straight trying to make it happen. 

So, yeah, it's more of a roller coaster. I don't really get stuck down in the dumps for weeks on end. It's more like these quick dips, mostly just because I'm so burnt out from everything else going on, and then I'm right back up again, running a million miles a minute. So no, not two weeks of just being depressed. It just doesn't stay that way for that long.

target_item.manifestation: Even during a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market, I still spent a few weeks believing people were tracking my buys and hearing the voice in the stockroom.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the voice (hallucinations) continued for at least two weeks while my mood was completely normal, which maps directly to Additional Requirement 3.

patient.answer:
Yeah, yeah, definitely. Like I said, it was that whole three or four-week stretch. That's definitely more than two weeks, right? So, yes. For that entire time, my mood was, you know, completely normal. I wasn't doing the two-hours-of-sleep thing, I wasn't running around the floor feeling like the king of the wholesale market, I wasn't snapping at the senior guys because they couldn't keep up with my brain. I was just... normal. Calm. Sleeping a solid seven or eight hours, coming in, drinking a normal amount of coffee, just doing my job. 

But even with all that calmness, even with my energy totally leveled out, I still spent that whole few weeks hearing the voice every time I went back into the stockroom. And it's not just the voice, either, it's the whole tracking thing. I spent that whole time, those few weeks, absolutely believing that people were tracking my buys on the terminal. I'd be sitting there, completely calm, heart rate totally fine, but I'd be digging through the network logs because I just knew someone had a keylogger on my system. I was so sure they were trying to steal my angles on the new drops. 

So, yeah, to answer your question, it definitely continued for at least two weeks. It was that whole three to four-week block where I felt totally fine, totally normal, but the voice and the paranoia about the tracking just... they just kept going. It's like my mood hit the brakes, but that other stuff just kept cruising right along at highway speeds. It's really hard to explain to someone who hasn't been there, you know? You're sitting there, feeling fine, but your brain is still telling you someone's talking to you in an empty room and someone's watching your every keystroke. It's wild. But yes, definitely for at least two weeks.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms occurred exclusively during mood episodes or also independently, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Before these problems started, had you ever heard voices or felt people were plotting against you when your mood was completely normal?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient experienced psychotic symptoms before the current problems started. While the profile indicates psychotic symptoms began 10 months ago, there is no specific item addressing the patient's history of these symptoms prior to the onset of the current illness.

patient.answer:
No, no, never. Honestly, before all this started happening recently, I never dealt with anything like that. I mean, I've always been a pretty regular guy, you know? Just went to high school, got my diploma, started working my way up in the wholesale business. I never had any weird stuff going on in my head. 

I remember back when I first started as a junior buyer—this was a couple years ago, way before any of this current mess—I was just focused on learning the ropes, figuring out how the purchase orders worked, getting to know the vendors. My mood was always just... normal. I'd go to work, do my hours, go home, watch some TV, hang out. I never heard anyone talking to me when I was alone in the stockroom back then. The stockroom was just quiet, you know? Just me and the boxes. 

And the whole tracking thing? Not even a blip on my radar back then. I used to just punch in my buys on the terminal, log off, and not give it a second thought. I never once worried that the senior guys or anyone else was trying to steal my angles or put keyloggers on my system. I just trusted the process. It's so crazy to think about how different it was. I was just a regular 22-year-old trying to make a living. So, yeah, before this whole recent situation with the wild energy and then the voices and the tracking... no, I never experienced anything like that when I was just feeling normal. It's all completely new, and honestly, it's pretty terrifying when you compare it to how quiet my life used to be.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have ever occurred exclusively outside mood episodes, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: At any point, did the voice start when your mood was completely normal, before any high or irritable period began?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The suspicious beliefs and the voice have been happening for roughly ten months now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the onset of the psychotic symptoms (the voice) relative to the mood episodes, which relates to how long the psychotic symptoms have been present (their duration).

patient.answer:
Well, let me think back... it's a little hard to untangle it all sometimes, you know? Because everything just kind of bleeds together when you're in the middle of it. But if I really sit down and trace it back... no, I don't think the voice or the tracking stuff started before the high energy kicked in. 

But, I mean, the whole thing—the voice in the stockroom, the absolute certainty that people are logging my keystrokes on the terminal, all of those suspicious beliefs—they've been going on for roughly ten months now. Ten whole months of this. It started around the end of last year, maybe? Yeah, about ten months. And it's just been this constant thing ever since, whether I'm bouncing off the walls and feeling like I own the wholesale market, or whether I'm in that calm, normal stretch like we were just talking about. 

It's just wild to think it's been almost a year of dealing with this. Ten months of looking over my shoulder at the terminal, ten months of dreading going into the stockroom because I know I'm going to hear it. It feels like a lifetime, honestly, but yeah, the timeline is right around ten months for all the suspicious stuff and the voice. But as for it starting *before* I ever got that initial crazy rush of energy and irritability? No, I'm pretty sure the super high energy kind of kicked the door open for everything else, and then the voice and the tracking fears just moved in and stayed for the last ten months.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least one month in total, to distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder and bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Altogether, have the voice and the feeling that people were plotting against you lasted for at least one full month?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The suspicious beliefs and the voice have been happening for roughly ten months now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking to confirm if the psychotic symptoms (the voice and suspicious beliefs) have lasted for at least one month, which directly corresponds to the duration of my psychotic symptoms.

patient.answer:
Oh, definitely. Like I was just saying a minute ago, it's been way, way longer than a month. I mean, honestly, I wish it had only been a month! A month I could probably handle, you know? Like, you can grit your teeth and get through a bad four weeks at the wholesale market. Like when the holiday shipments get backed up or a major vendor screws up a purchase order, you just put your head down and push through it for a month. 

But this isn't just a bad month. Like I mentioned, the suspicious beliefs and the voice have been happening for roughly ten months now. Ten whole months. When you really sit down and think about how many days that actually is... how many times I've had to walk into that stockroom to check inventory and just brace myself, waiting to hear it. Or how many times I've sat at my terminal, totally convinced someone is logging my keystrokes to steal my purchase angles and sabotage my numbers. It's exhausting just talking about it. Ten months of looking over my shoulder every single shift, trying to figure out who's plotting against me while I'm just trying to do my job. 

So, yeah, if you're asking if it's been at least one full month, the answer is a massive yes. It's basically been almost a year of my life just swallowed up by this stuff, day in and day out, whether my mood is totally fine or I'm bouncing off the walls. Ten months of it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms persisted for at least two weeks in the absence of mood symptoms, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you had at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice while your mood felt completely normal?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market, I still spent a few weeks believing people were tracking my buys and hearing the voice in the stockroom.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the hallucinations (hearing the voice) occurred for at least two weeks while my mood was completely normal, which directly matches the criterion for delusions and hallucinations occurring in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Yeah, yeah I have. Actually, it's funny you ask about that specific timeframe, because I was just thinking about this stretch... I guess it was a little while back, maybe a couple months ago? I remember it really clearly because, for a second there, I thought maybe I was getting better, or at least getting back to my old self. My energy had finally leveled out. I wasn't waking up at 3 AM with a million ideas for new vendor contracts, and I wasn't talking a mile a minute to the senior buyers. I was actually sleeping through the night, getting a solid seven or eight hours, which was huge for me. I felt... calm. Just normal, regular calm. Not like I was running the whole wholesale market single-handedly, just going in, doing my job, grabbing lunch at the deli across the street, coming back. 

But the thing is, even though my mood was totally fine, completely baseline, the other stuff didn't stop. Not at all. For that whole stretch—it was definitely a few weeks, maybe three or four weeks of just feeling totally regular mood-wise—I was still absolutely convinced that they were tracking my buys on the terminal. I'd sit there, feeling totally calm, but still knowing, just knowing, that someone had a keylogger on my system, watching every purchase order I punched in. And the voice in the stockroom? Still there. I'd go back there to check on a shipment of overstock, feeling completely rested and normal, and I'd still hear it. Just as clear as day. 

It was almost more disturbing that way, honestly. When you're all keyed up and your thoughts are racing, the weird stuff almost fits the vibe, you know? But when you're just sitting there, sipping a coffee, feeling totally fine, and you still hear someone talking to you in an empty room, or you're still terrified to type on your own keyboard... it really messes with your head. So, yeah, there was definitely a period of a few weeks where my mood was totally normal, but the tracking fears and the voice just kept right on going. It didn't take a break just because my energy did.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms persisted for at least two weeks in the absence of any mood episode, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: During that three- to four-week period when your mood felt completely normal, did the voice continue the whole time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market, I still spent a few weeks believing people were tracking my buys and hearing the voice in the stockroom.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the hallucination (the voice) persisted continuously during the period of normal mood, which addresses the criterion of psychotic symptoms occurring in the absence of a major mood episode for at least two weeks.

patient.answer:
Yeah, yeah, it did. The whole time. Like, every single day of that three or four-week stretch. It’s so strange to think about, really, because you’d assume—or at least I assumed—that if my mood leveled out, if I was finally getting a decent night’s sleep and not waking up at all hours feeling like I had to single-handedly restructure the entire wholesale market... you’d think the other stuff would just fade away, right? Like it was all tied together. 

But it wasn't. Even during that calmer stretch, when I was actually sleeping normally and going into work without that frantic, electric energy... I was still spending all my time believing people were tracking my buys. I’d sit down at my desk with my morning coffee, feeling totally rested, totally fine, and I’d still be staring at the keyboard, absolutely certain someone had rigged it. And the stockroom... man, the stockroom didn't change at all. I’d walk back there to do a routine inventory check, completely calm, not agitated in the slightest, and there it was. The voice. Just as clear as if someone was standing right behind me. 

It didn’t take a day off. Not once during those weeks. It’s almost like... like the voice and the tracking stuff have a mind of their own, completely separate from how I’m actually feeling in my own head. It’s exhausting, honestly, because it makes you realize that even when you feel like you’re doing better, you’re not really free of it. You’re just dealing with it while being less energetic. So, yes, to answer your question, it continued the entire time. Every day of those few weeks, without fail.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least one month in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: At any point, did you hear the voice for a full month while your mood felt completely normal?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market, I still spent a few weeks believing people were tracking my buys and hearing the voice in the stockroom.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the hallucinations (hearing the voice) occurred for a full month in the absence of mood symptoms, which relates to the duration of psychotic symptoms without a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Well, a full month? No, I wouldn't say it was a full month. Like I was just saying, it was more like a few weeks. Maybe three or four weeks at the most where my mood was just... regular. Baseline. You know, that stretch where I was finally getting some decent sleep and not waking up feeling like I had to conquer the entire wholesale market before sunrise. 

But even during that calmer stretch, even when I wasn't running on that crazy, electric energy, I still spent those few weeks absolutely convinced that people were tracking my buys on the terminal. And the voice in the stockroom was still there, too. But it wasn't a whole month of feeling normal while that stuff was happening. It was just those few weeks. Because eventually, my mood shifted again. It always does, right? You get this little window where you think, "Okay, I'm just a regular guy going to work, grabbing a sandwich, coming home," but then the energy starts creeping back up, or I get completely dragged down. 

So, no, not a full month of normal mood. Just that three- or four-week window where my energy was fine, but I was still dealing with the tracking and the voice every single day. It's like they're on their own schedule, completely ignoring whether I'm feeling balanced or not. But yeah, the normal mood part? That didn't last a whole month. Just a few weeks.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has ever had a major depressive episode, which would support schizoaffective disorder over bipolar I disorder with psychotic features or schizophrenia.
doctor.question: During the past year, have you ever had two weeks in a row when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a major depressive episode (feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day for two weeks), but my symptom profile does not include a symptom for depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Depressed? Like, really down for two weeks straight? No, I don't think so. Not for two weeks in a row, anyway. I mean, sure, I get bummed out sometimes, who doesn't? Especially in wholesale, it can be a real grind, you know? You're constantly dealing with vendors who promise one thing and deliver another, or the logistics get messed up, and you're just sitting there at your desk feeling like you're banging your head against a brick wall. And honestly, dealing with all the tracking stuff... the keylogger on my terminal, the feeling that someone is always watching my purchase orders... that can really drag a guy down. It gets exhausting, it really does. 

There are definitely days where I just feel totally wiped out by it all, where I just want to put my head down on the desk and not talk to anyone. But it's never been like, two solid weeks of just feeling depressed all day, every day. It's more like I'll have a bad day or two where I'm just fed up and tired, but then the energy comes back. Usually, the energy comes back pretty strong, actually. I'll go from feeling totally drained to suddenly realizing I need to overhaul the entire inventory system right this second, and I'll be up for three days straight trying to make it happen. 

So, yeah, it's more of a roller coaster. I don't really get stuck down in the dumps for weeks on end. It's more like these quick dips, mostly just because I'm so burnt out from everything else going on, and then I'm right back up again, running a million miles a minute. So no, not two weeks of just being depressed. It just doesn't stay that way for that long.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes clear manic episodes lasting well over 1 week with decreased need for sleep, elevated/irritable mood, increased energy, grandiosity, and behavioral dyscontrol, alongside persistent psychotic symptoms (persecutory delusions and auditory hallucinations). Crucially, hallucinations and delusional beliefs continued for at least 2 weeks during a period of completely normal mood, which supports schizoaffective disorder, manic type, over bipolar I disorder with psychotic symptoms. Schizophrenia was considered, but mood episodes have been present for the majority of the illness duration, favoring schizoaffective disorder.
